item.title: Gozan no Okuribi: Kyoto's Great Bonfire Farewell — Guide
item.description: Gozan no Okuribi, popularly called Daimonji, is one of Kyoto’s most solemn and spectacular annual events, held on the night of 16 August to close the Obon festival, when the spirits of ancestors are believed to return to the other world. On five mountains encircling the city, huge bonfires are lit in the shape of characters and forms — most famously the giant character for ‘great’, dai, blazing on Mount Nyoigatake above the eastern hills — each ignited in turn over the course of an hour.
